note: Derived from Brandle, Stocks, Tenenbaum, Gershman & Schulz (2023), Nature Human Behaviour 7:1481-1489. The published dataset is 'Little Alchemy 2': 29,493 online players, 4,691,033 attempted combinations, 720 reachable elements from 4 starting elements. Figure 1c reports mean 158.06 trials (s.d. 695.38) and mean final inventory 50.91 elements (s.d. 76.42) per player. novelty_rate is therefore (50.91 - 4) / 158.06 = 0.297, SUPERSEDING the previous 0.35. CAVEATS a reviewer should be told: (1) 'Tiny Alchemy' is a separate validation experiment in the authors' repository (additionalexperiments/), not the headline study, so this port's name matches the variant while its baseline comes from the main dataset; (2) the reported distributions are extremely skewed (s.d. 695 on a mean of 158 trials; 563 players exceeded 1,000 trials), so a z-score against a single SD is a poor summary and the sd here is NOT derived from the paper; (3) success_rate 0.40 and unique_pair_rate 0.95 remain author estimates - the paper reports neither a per-player success rate nor a repeat-attempt rate.
